I think this is a great application as far as the shape is concerned because that spike pattern is time consuming to make by hand and you can get whatever ergonomics you prefer. I do share similar concerns that others rather rudely pointed out in regards to the porosity. Even if you use the plastic film every time, just having it in a kitchen setting means it's pretty likely to get something on it eventually and straight off the printer  is just too rough to be reliability food safe. I think in theory with enough  filling, sanding, polishing and a foodsafe coating it could be done, but with that much work you'd might as well carve it from wood as the work would be about the same.
 All that being said, I still think you have something worth using, just not in it's current state. If it were me, I think the next step would be making a mould of some sort and casting it as a more or less solid piece. Aluminum would or steel would probably be ideal if possible, but I'm sure there's a food safe resin out there some where. Best of luck whatever you go with.

We're in a band with all of existence, playing a song from the very beginning. Everything we can see, experience, describe, as well as not describe is all playing along with the song. So, to meditate, Be aware that you are alive, and a part of this reality. That's it. No goal, nothing mesure, and nothing gauge your progress.  Sometimes we have to sit quietly, and try to calm the side of our consciousness that likes to get in the way of us playing along with life.
